correctness.rationale: A bounded real-linear extension preserves constants, hence new-origin functional has weights summing to one. Averaging over signed coordinate permutations gives uniform mean with no greater seminorm norm. For each vertex v, |mean(f)−f(v)|≤mean ρ(v,u) exactly saturated by the 1-Lipschitz distance-to-v function; this proves the universal OPTIMAL norm max(1,F_d). The finite binomial formula is exact. For d≥2, F_d(0+)=1−2^-d<1, F_d(1)>1, F_d′′(α)>0; the crossing is unique. For K~Bin(d,1/2), μ_d=E[log(2sqrt(K/d))1_{K>0}]=.5log2−1/(4d)+O(d^-2) using symmetric binomial moments/tail control; Taylor at α=O(2^-d) gives 2^d α_d=2/log2 +1/((log2)^2 d)+O(d^-2). For α=1, centered-binomial expansion yields sqrt2(1−1/(8d)+O(d^-2)). Independently computed thresholds α_2≈0.611516173, α_3≈0.352841879, α_4≈0.191981864; finite tests not a proof for all d. The d=1 exclusion and α→0+ limit are sound.
